progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: C6a, C6b and C8 (with C1 to C7) and Year 11: the three calculation types and ICE tables (I for initial, C for change, E for equilibrium) with the measured value in the Equilibrium row first (C6a); x from the coefficients, the perfect-square root, the tiny-K drop with its 5 per cent check, and multiply both sides by the bottom then divide (C6b); Q and the Q against K rule (C8); the effect of adding a reactant (C3); c = n / V, square and cube roots and powers of ten. Nothing about huge-K shortcuts or addition problems is assumed.
progression.startsWith: Three types of calculation from the C6 videos, two more that turn up in HSC questions, five in all.
progression.stopsAfter: Naming all five types from what a question gives and asks; the huge-K shortcut with its check, including a one-sentence reactant-start case; an amount-added problem in a vessel that is not 1 L, answered in moles. Types 1, 2 and 4 and the perfect-square and tiny-K cases are recalled, not re-taught; no colorimetry, no temperature dependence of K.
progression.nextLesson: G03c: equilibrium calculations, HSC-style practice, part 1.

teaching.task: Tell which of the five types an equilibrium calculation is from what it gives and asks, and do the two cases not met before: a huge K and an amount added.
teaching.causalExplanation: What a question gives and what it asks decide the type. With K and a start the change is x; a tiny K means hardly any reactant changes, so x is dropped from start minus x and tested. A huge K is the mirror image: the reaction runs almost fully to products, so the small unknown is what is left of the reactants, tested the same way. An addition changes Q and leaves K alone, so the added substance goes in the initial row as the old equilibrium plus y, the new value goes in the Equilibrium row first and gives the change, the added substance is also used up in the change row, and the old K is reused; y in mol/L is multiplied by the volume to give moles.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens by saying the C6 videos met three types and two more turn up in HSC questions, naming all five once with what each gives and finds and where it was taught, recalls the tiny-K drop in one line so the huge K can mirror it, works the huge-K case and the amount-added example one stage per scene with a try-it, and closes with a You see and You do board of all five types and a handoff to the practice set.
teaching.openingDecision: Every HSC equilibrium calculation is one of five types. Which one do you have, and what do you do first?
teaching.understandingCheck: For CO + H2O = CO2 + H2 with K = 4.00 in 2.00 L, steam is added to an equilibrium of 0.400, 0.400, 0.800 and 0.800 mol and the new equilibrium has 0.200 mol CO: solve 0.500 x 0.500 / (0.100 (0.100 + y)) = 4.00 for y, and give the moles of steam added.
teaching.curriculumScope: Calculate equilibrium constants and equilibrium concentrations from supplied data, including after a change to an equilibrium mixture, and use Q to predict direction (Module 5). Every question is written for HSCScience and is not presented as an official question. Types 1, 2 and 4 are named, with the teaching in C6a and C8; marks allocation, colorimetry, temperature dependence of K, Ksp and acid calculations are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, the C6a type cards extended to five with lit, ticked and dim states and a You see and You do table, the C6 ICE table with the equilibrium-row-first pen arrow and E minus I bracket, the C5 expression builder, the C6 algebra line, the C6b check ruler and tiny-K thumbnail, and a coded reactant-start diagram. Colour key as C2 to C8: forward blue, reverse amber, equal teal, made plus green, used up minus red.
design.transitionPlan: The five-card column sets the lesson; card 3 shrinks to a badge for the tiny-K recall and a mirror line leads into the huge-K board; the C6b ruler returns for the huge-K test; the amount-added example runs across four boards with the table and equation kept; the five cards return and open into the You see and You do table; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.visualReference: The C6a type cards extended to a five-card column, each with a one-line given and find and a tag for where it was taught (C6a, C6b, C8), sub-chips on card 3 for perfect square, tiny K and huge K, ticks for the taught types and the huge-K chip and card 5 lit as today
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the full map: three types from the C6 videos plus two more, each named once by what it gives and what it finds, so the learner knows which parts are recall and which are new

scenes.motionPurpose: Three cards slide in, two more join to make five, each card writes its given and find line on its cue, taught cards tick with their video tag, and the huge-K chip and card 5 light as today
scenes.onScreenChange: Heading "What you are given and asked decides the type" writes on; on "three types" three cards slide in; on "five in all" two more join and the column numbers 1 to 5; each card writes its given and find line on its cue (card 2 shows "I initial, C change, E equilibrium"); cards 1 and 2 tick on "first C6 video" with the tag "C6a"; card 3 gains sub-chips "perfect square" and "tiny K" ticked on "second C6 video" (tag "C6b") and a lit "huge K" chip tagged "today" on "huge K"; card 4 ticks on "Q video" (tag "C8, the Q video"); card 5 lights on "added" with "today"

scenes.visualReference: Card 3 shrinking to a type badge, a C6b tiny-K thumbnail (I2 = 2I) with the start minus x sliding out, the C6b check ruler at 0.4 per cent with a tick, and a faint mirror line with an empty huge K half
scenes.teachingReason: Recalls the tiny-K drop and its test from C6b so that the recorded "A huge K is the mirror image" in the next scene has something to mirror
scenes.narrationCue: Type three / tiny K / dropped it / tested it
scenes.motionPurpose: Card 3 shrinks to a badge, the C6b line writes and its minus x slides out, the ruler ticks under 5 per cent, and a mirror line draws with an empty right half
scenes.onScreenChange: Card 3 shrinks to the badge "Type 3: K + start"; on "tiny K" the thumbnail "I2 = 2I, K = 1.6 x 10^-5, start 0.25 mol/L" (tag "from C6b") writes; on "dropped it" "0.25 - x = 0.25 (approx.)" writes as the "- x" slides out; on "tested it" the check ruler shows "x = 0.0010: 0.4%" under the dashed 5 per cent line with a tick and the chip "Test it or don't use it"; a faint mirror line draws with an empty right half labelled "huge K?"

scenes.visualReference: A fresh board with the 2SO2 + O2 = 2SO3 strip, a givens card with a huge K and a product-only start, and an ICE table with signs reversed
scenes.teachingReason: Sets up the mirror case: with a huge K and a product start almost nothing splits
scenes.narrationCue: huge K / 4.0 times ten to the ten / oxygen / two x / about 0.400
scenes.motionPurpose: The board builds, the ICE table fills with plus 2x, plus x and minus 2x, and the last cell shades to about 0.400 with a tag about how little splits
scenes.onScreenChange: Task "Find [O2] at equilibrium", the equation, and the givens card "K = 4.0 x 10^10", "start: [SO3] = 0.400 mol/L, no SO2, no O2" with the two tags appear; the table fills Initial 0, 0, 0.400; Change +2x, +x, -2x; Equilibrium 2x, x, 0.400 - 2x with the last cell shaded to about 0.400 and the tag "K is very large; test how little SO3 splits"

scenes.visualReference: The C5 builder writing K for the product start and the working in beats down to x cubed, with an unspoken crossed (2x)^2 chip
scenes.teachingReason: Solves the huge-K case with each step shown
scenes.narrationCue: 0.160 / one times ten to the minus twelve / one times ten to the minus four / x cubed
scenes.motionPurpose: The expression builds and the working writes in beats to x = 1.0 x 10^-4
scenes.onScreenChange: The builder writes K; the working writes "0.400^2 / ((2x)^2 x) = 4.0 x 10^10", "0.160 / 4x^3 = 0.040 / x^3", "x^3 = 0.040 / (4.0 x 10^10) = 1.0 x 10^-12", "x = 1.0 x 10^-4 mol/L" with the tag "K: no unit written"; an unspoken crossed chip "(2x)^2 = 2x^2" appears; beside the x^3 line a small pen tag "multiply both sides by the bottom, then divide" writes

scenes.visualReference: The check ruler with 2x against 0.400 at 0.05 per cent, then a coded mini diagram of reactants running all the way to products with a small x bar returning
scenes.teachingReason: Tests the huge-K shortcut and states the reactant-start case in one sentence
scenes.narrationCue: Test it / 0.00020 / Now the other way round / started with just the reactants / products / back / An excess of one reactant would stay
scenes.motionPurpose: The ruler shows 2x as a hair against the start, the final concentrations write, and a mini diagram shows reactants going to products with a small x taken back
scenes.onScreenChange: The ruler shows 2x = 0.00020 against 0.400 at "0.05%" under the 5 per cent line with a tick; the final line "[O2] = 1.0 x 10^-4 mol/L, [SO2] = 2.0 x 10^-4 mol/L" writes; on "started with just the reactants" a mini diagram shows 2SO2 + O2 running all the way to 2SO3 with a dashed arrow and a small bar "take x back" returning; the tag about reactants in the equation ratio and an excess reactant staying appears

scenes.visualReference: A fresh board with the CO + H2O = CO2 + H2 strip, a grouped givens card of old and new amounts, and the amounts dividing into a mol/L column
scenes.teachingReason: Starts the worked example for the hardest type: reads the question and converts every amount to concentration
scenes.narrationCue: amount added / 2.00 litre / convert / 0.200 moles / The new carbon monoxide is 0.100
scenes.motionPurpose: The givens card builds line by line, the old amounts divide by 2.00 into a mol/L column and the new carbon monoxide converts to 0.100
scenes.onScreenChange: Task "How many moles of steam were added?", the equation and the grouped givens card appear with the tag "HSC-style question, written for HSCScience"; on "convert" the old amounts divide by 2.00 into a mol/L column (0.200, 0.200, 0.400, 0.400) and the new CO converts to 0.100 mol/L; the chip "Concentrations, not moles" shows

scenes.visualReference: The C6 ICE table with CO, H2O, CO2 and H2 columns, a caption over the Initial row, y written in the pen colour with an added-steam icon, the E minus I bracket and 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 coefficient chips
scenes.teachingReason: Shows why y sits in the initial row, how the measured value gives the first change and how the other changes follow
scenes.narrationCue: Right after the steam goes in / initial row / plus y / equilibrium row / minus 0.100 / used up
scenes.motionPurpose: A caption names the instant after adding, y writes into the steam cell, the pen arrow and bracket give the CO change, the chips fly in and the equilibrium row completes
scenes.onScreenChange: The caption "the instant after adding, before anything reacts: old equilibrium + y" appears over the Initial row; the row ticks 0.200, "0.200 + y", 0.400, 0.400 with y and the label "y = steam added, mol/L"; the pen arrow puts 0.100 into the CO Equilibrium cell and the "E - I" bracket with "0.100 - 0.200" gives "-0.100"; the chips "1 : 1 : 1 : 1" fill H2O -0.100, CO2 +0.100, H2 +0.100; the Equilibrium row completes "0.100 + y", 0.500, 0.500; a ghost crossed chip "y in the change row" fades; the aid "The added substance goes in the initial row" writes

scenes.visualReference: The C5 builder with the equilibrium cells dropping in, the equation 0.500 x 0.500 over 0.100 x (0.100 + y) = 4.00, and the question y = ? with the countdown ring
scenes.teachingReason: Sets up the K equation and lets the learner solve for y before the answer
scenes.narrationCue: 0.100 plus y / K has not changed / 4.00 / moles per litre / Pause here and try it
scenes.motionPurpose: The expression builds, the equilibrium values drop in, the equation writes and y = ? holds with the countdown ring
scenes.onScreenChange: The builder writes the K expression and the equilibrium cells drop in; "0.500 x 0.500 / (0.100 x (0.100 + y)) = 4.00" writes with the tag "K: no unit written"; the question "y = ? mol/L" holds with the countdown ring and "Pause here and try it." written beside it; no values for y are shown
scenes.holdPurpose: 10 second answer-free countdown after "Pause here and try it."

scenes.visualReference: The working writing in beats to y = 0.525 mol/L and 1.05 mol, a teal K check, two crossed wrong-answer chips with pen arrows and a silent Q mini number line
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the answer in moles, checks it and names the two classic slips
scenes.motionPurpose: The working writes to 0.525 mol/L, multiplies by 2.00 L to 1.05 mol, the independent check ticks in teal and the two wrong chips are crossed with arrows to their causes
scenes.onScreenChange: The working writes "0.500 x 0.500 = 0.250", "0.100 + y = 0.250 / (4.00 x 0.100) = 0.625", "y = 0.525 mol/L", then "0.525 mol/L x 2.00 L = 1.05 mol" with a tick; the check "0.250 / (0.100 x 0.625) = 4.00" gets a teal "= K" tick; the chips "0.525 (mol/L, not mol): volume forgotten" and "0.425 mol/L: steam used up not counted" are crossed with arrows to the 2.00 L and the -0.100 cell; a silent mini number line shows Q at 1.10 below K = 4.00; the aid chip "Initial row: plus y. K stays." lands; beside the "0.100 + y" line a small pen tag "multiply both sides by the bottom, then divide" writes

scenes.teachingReason: Leaves the learner with the full five-type map tied to the wording that signals each type, and hands off to the practice set
